terms.gloss: put the finishing touches to, complete
evidence: Quint. prooem. 4: quasi perfectīs summam ēloquentiae manum impōnerent, gave the last touch to (Lewis & Short s.v. impōnō)
Plin. NH 36.5.16: summam manum operī (Lewis & Short s.v. impōnō)
terms.comment: Latin speaks of the last hand laid on a work: Cicero says of an unfinished work manus extrēma nōn accessit (Brut. 33.126, Lewis & Short s.v. manus), and Virgil has extrēmam bellō impōnere manum (A. 7.573). Traupman also offers ultimam manum impōnere; Petronius has a poem that nōndum recēpit ultimam manum (118, Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: manus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 396.
